artifacts.summary: Maps all 5 WORK items to concrete file/line locations across the 9 declared consumer files; confirms task 59's predicate half is complete and live at schema v5 with idle_overlap_advisory already implemented; identifies the exact false self-clearing claim in skill-orchestrate/SKILL.md (line ~1538-1542) and the three-way corpus disagreement it creates; flags one open design question (--allow-scope-collision bypass scope: both collision_scope values vs. cross_batch only) and one likely-in-scope-by-inclusion item (orchestrate-dry-run-report.sh's missing idle_overlap_advisory rendering, not explicitly named in WORK 1's prose but in the declared file_scope).

memory_candidates.content: In this repo's orchestrate-batch-admit.sh subsystem, consumer-facing docs distinguish 'dispatch-path warning' (the live admission gate at skill-orchestrate/SKILL.md Stage MT-3 step 4.5, and its illustrative twin in commands/orchestrate.md) from a separate, earlier 'pre-dispatch review' surface (Step 1.5, orchestrate-predispatch-review.sh) that is advisory-loud but never blocking and runs on the full raw dependencies[] before wave narrowing. A gap named 'lives in a separate review surface rather than where the exclusion is actually reported' means: the review script already computes/prints a finding, but the actual defer/exclusion site (a different file, later in execution) doesn't repeat it — the fix folds the SAME computed string into the second site rather than building new logic.

skill-orchestrate/SKILL.md and skill-orchestrate-hard/SKILL.md are explicit co-maintenance twins for the multi-task admission gate (file header states 'an edit to either copy REQUIRES the same edit to the other'). The hard-mode file sometimes takes a shortcut of saying 'unchanged from the base skill's handling' for a branch instead of transcribing it fully (e.g. its file_scope_collision bullet) — when the base skill's prose for that branch is corrected, the hard-mode file's shortcut pointer becomes stale/wrong too and must either be updated to match or converted into a full transcription, not just left as 'no change needed'.
